In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the remodeling of the leg neuromotor system during metamorphosis is characterized by the loss and subsequent re-establishment of synaptic specializations in the terminal processes of motoneurons.
presynaptic specialisations are not lost in insect metamorphosis, rather they are transiently distributed along the axon shafts and then reappear at the terminals of the motoneuron.

the presynaptic machinery is not only maintained in the motoneurons but is also capable of re-establishing presynaptic active zones in a dynamic manner during the remodeling of the neuromuscular junction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the larval neuromuscular synapse is not simply a degenerating structure, but a dynamic system that is actively remodeled to support the formation of new adult neuromuscular junctions.

presynaptic function is not restricted to the nerve terminals but is widely distributed throughout the nerve branches, and that this function is not lost during muscle fiber degeneration but is re-established as the new muscle forms.
presynaptic function is not a static process but is dynamic and is regulated by both intrinsic and extrinsic factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
presynaptic terminals are not fixed in position and that the same neuron can form presynaptic specializa- tions at different locations in response to changing conditions in the target muscle.
presynaptic function persists during muscle remodeling, and it can be detected by both immunohistochemical and functional methods.
the presynaptic machinery is present in axons and is functional in the absence of the target muscle, suggesting that the presynapse may be a more independent structure than was previously thought.
